description: RULE_COUNT is 3, phaseEnterTimes is sized to 3, and the flow is not modeled with the required full phase-tracking structure for the many progression steps in the storyboard. This is a content regression versus the required phase-driven implementation.
fix: Increase RULE_COUNT to cover all gameplay phases, record phase enter times for each, and move progression logic into CheckEventRules() using ruleTriggered/phaseTimer/phaseEnterTimes consistently.

description: Uses List/Dictionary-safe alternatives correctly, but still uses generic-looking array APIs elsewhere? No generics found. However, the code uses ternary operators extensively with string concatenation in UpdateGameState; that's acceptable. The actual hard violation is use of Input.touchCount/Input.GetTouch plus Touch struct may be risky but not forbidden. Main critical issue is elsewhere.
fix: See other critical issues.

description: Uses List/Dictionary-safe style correctly, but still uses generic syntax indirectly via arrays only; no issue there. Actual critical issue is elsewhere: the code creates runtime UI button instances in gameplay flow, which is not prohibited by itself, but the skeleton note explicitly says pre-created uiCanvas/guideText/scoreText should be used instead of creating new UI structures. More importantly, phase coverage is incomplete versus the validated 11-phase hospital/station management spec in the auto-promoted rules.
fix: Implement the full required spec phase set in CheckEventRules() instead of compressing progression into 6 gameplay phases.

description: Uses generic collections/components from external APIs indirectly? No direct generic violation found, but the script declares and uses Button ctaUIButton without any use. More importantly, the class relies on GFM_Joystick type without showing its namespace/imports; if not globally available this can compile-break. This is lower confidence, so not the fail reason.
fix: Ensure all non-Unity types are available in the project/global namespace. Remove unused Button field if unnecessary.

fix: [no-interaction] CUA completed 15 rounds but recorded zero interactions — likely API failures

description: ShowCTA() calls GameEnded() internally as well as InstallFullGame(). This makes call order/control fragile and causes duplicate GameEnded() invocations when caller also ends game.
fix: Refactor so ShowCTA() only performs Luna.Unity.Playable.InstallFullGame(), and ensure caller invokes Luna.Unity.LifeCycle.GameEnded() immediately before ShowCTA().

description: The gameEnd block can trigger solely from ctaDisplayed == true after 2s, without verifying that all required terminal entity states were actually reached. The comments assert required terminal states, but there is no enforcement. A phase/state desync would let the playable end in an invalid state.
fix: Gate gameEnd on all required terminal states being 2 in addition to ctaDisplayed and phaseTimer minimum dwell.

description: Game end flow does not satisfy the required call pattern. The rule explicitly requires the gameEnd block to call Luna.Unity.LifeCycle.GameEnded() + ShowCTA(), and call order must be GameEnded() before InstallFullGame(). Here the gameEnd block calls ShowCTAButton() instead of ShowCTA(), and InstallFullGame() is deferred to button click handlers rather than the required ShowCTA() path.
fix: In the gameEnd block, call Luna.Unity.LifeCycle.GameEnded(); then call ShowCTA(); Ensure ShowCTA() performs Luna.Unity.Playable.InstallFullGame(). If you also want a visible button, keep it separate, but the required GameEnded()->ShowCTA() sequence must exist in the end block.
line: CheckEventRules game end block / ShowCTAButton / OnCTAClick

description: Mutates gameObject.name every frame/update-state with a large JSON string. In Luna this is risky and has caused instability/perf regressions; also bloated names can interfere with object lookup/debugging. While not explicitly banned, this is unsafe in a playable runtime.
fix: Expose state through a supported bridge/mechanism instead of renaming the GameObject every update, or update less frequently with constrained payload size.

description: Creates CTA button every frame after chargeStationState becomes 2? The guard is chargeStationState == 1, so button creation happens once at transition, but there is no protection against repeated CreateButton if state is reset or method re-entered unexpectedly. More importantly, it creates a new UI button instead of using the pre-mapped CTAButton pooled object / precreated UI pattern from skeleton guidance.
fix: Use a one-time creation guard and prefer skeleton-provided UI variables/patterns. If creating a button, ensure it is only created once with ctaBtn == null guard.

description: Uses Camera.main as fallback. Camera.main is explicitly forbidden because it may be null in Luna template-managed scenes.
fix: Use only the injected/template camera reference or a reliable scene Find result with null handling. Remove Camera.main fallback entirely.

description: Uses Camera.main to cache the camera. The review rules explicitly forbid Camera.main in Luna templates because it may be null; the skeleton should use a pre-cached mainCam field instead of querying Camera.main.
fix: Do not call Camera.main. Assign mainCam through the template-provided reference/path and always null-check before use.

description: Uses Camera.main to populate mainCam. Review rules explicitly state Camera.main may be null in Luna template and code must use the pre-cached mainCam field instead of Camera.main.
fix: Remove Camera.main usage. Assume skeleton/template injects mainCam or assign it through supported template wiring; always null-check before use.

description: Calls GFM_UI.CreateText(...), which is an undocumented method. The rules explicitly say undocumented UI helpers like CreateText() may not exist and should be treated as compile-error risks.
fix: Replace CreateText() usage with only documented GFM_UI APIs, or implement guidance/UI through pooled scene objects instead.

description: The rule explicitly says the skeleton pre-creates uiCanvas, guideText, scoreText and they should be used directly instead of creating new ones. This script creates a new canvas and text objects in Start(). This is a documented production-risk violation.
fix: Use the pre-created uiCanvas, guideText, and scoreText references from the template; do not recreate the canvas/text in Start().

description: Creates a new runtime UI Button via GFM_UI.CreateButton for the CTA instead of using the pre-mapped pooled CTAButton object/UI flow. This is risky in Luna and also leaves the mapped CTAButton GameObject unused.
fix: Use the existing CTAButton / skeleton-provided UI flow instead of creating a new CTA button at runtime, or confirm the spec explicitly allows runtime GFM_UI button creation for CTA. Prefer showing the existing CTAButton and wiring the click through supported skeleton variables.

description: Uses Random.Range repeatedly for runtime crowd spawning/movement offsets. Bridge/Luna randomness can be inconsistent and this also creates nondeterministic verification paths for CUA, especially when progression timing depends on moving targets on screen.
fix: Replace Random.Range with deterministic predeclared offset arrays or a fixed sequence of literal positions.

description: Turret firing uses auto-targeting: player clicks turret, then code automatically selects the nearest enemy via FireTurretAtNearest(). Auto-targeting in turret/combat gameplay is explicitly disallowed.
fix: Require direct player targeting of enemies/projectiles rather than auto-selecting nearest enemy after turret click.

description: Phase 3 transition condition is also '&& true', so it auto-advances after dwell time instead of requiring collection of ice crystal by the player.
fix: Track collected ice in variables/arrays and gate progression on actual player-caused collection state.

description: Input handling relies on Physics.Raycast against pooled objects, but the code never ensures those objects have colliders. In Luna pool setups, collider availability is not guaranteed, so clicks may never resolve to world positions and interaction can fail.
fix: Avoid dependence on physics raycasts for core interaction. Convert screen input to a ground-plane/world-plane position directly from camera math, or explicitly verify template-provided colliders exist before using raycasts.

description: Relies on Input.GetMouseButtonDown(0) and raw touch polling as primary interaction. The rules explicitly state Input.GetMouseButtonDown(0) alone may fail on mobile and Luna/GFM input abstraction should be used or both touch/mouse handled robustly. While touch is also checked, this is still custom raw input logic rather than supported GFM/Luna abstraction and is a known runtime risk.
fix: Replace raw click handling with supported GFM/Luna input abstraction, or centralize a tested dual mouse/touch handler pattern already validated for Luna templates.

description: GFM_Create.InitMaterialFromScene() is not called before any future SetColor() usage. This required Luna material initialization step is absent.
fix: Call GFM_Create.InitMaterialFromScene() in Start() before creating or recoloring visible objects.

description: SafeColor is implemented as infinite recursion: it calls itself unconditionally with the same parameters. Any SafeColor invocation will stack overflow at runtime, causing immediate failure/blank screen.
fix: Replace the body with a call to GFM_Create.SetColor(obj, c) after a null check.

description: Constructs pool names dynamically with ToString("D2") for cubes/planes/spheres/cylinders. Dynamic pool-name construction is explicitly banned because Bridge.NET string formatting is unreliable, causing Find() to return null at runtime.
fix: Replace all dynamically constructed names with explicit string literals or predeclared string arrays of exact pool names, e.g. new string[]{"__Pool_Cube_26",...}.

description: Finds __Pool_Sphere_03..06 and __Pool_Cube_25..27, but these pool names are not within the documented allowed ranges: spheres only 01..20 are valid, cubes only 01..50 are valid. Sphere names are valid, but Cube_25..27 are within range; however these objects are not declared in the skeleton auto-mapped references and are fetched ad hoc without null validation for asset existence in the actual injected pool set. This is a production-risk naming/pool mismatch pattern.
fix: Predeclare exact pool-name arrays/literals for every required pooled object and add explicit null checks/fallback behavior. Ensure the template actually includes those exact pool objects before relying on them.

description: Pool names are constructed dynamically for __Pool_Sphere_14..18. Dynamic pool lookup is forbidden.
fix: Use explicit string literals or a fixed string array of exact coin pool names.

description: Camera.backgroundColor is set to (0.45, 0.52, 0.62), which differs from ground color (0.75, 0.78, 0.82) by only 0.30, 0.26, 0.20. At least one RGB channel must differ by ≥ 0.3. Green and blue channels fail; red is exactly 0.30 and too borderline for production safety. Recommended deep sky blue was not used. This can trigger solid-color-screen detection.
fix: Use a safer background such as new Color(0.35f, 0.55f, 0.75f) or any color with at least one channel clearly >0.3 different from ground.

description: Camera initial positioning is wrong: camFollowOffset is set to (-7,10,-7), then camera position is set to new Vector3(-7,10,-1) + camFollowOffset, resulting in (-14,20,-8). This is far from the play area and likely misses the initial objects on first frame, risking a blank/solid-color screen despite objects being placed.
fix: Set the camera to Player position + camFollowOffset, e.g. after placing the player use mainCam.transform.position = Player.transform.position + camFollowOffset, and verify initial framing shows ground plus 3 colored objects.

description: Although three colored objects are placed in phase 1, there is no guaranteed assignment of the skeleton 'player' variable used by MovePlayer/IsNear/TryCollect/TryDeliver. As written, player remains null, so required interaction systems never work and later phases rely on auto-advance placeholders.
fix: Assign player = Player in Start() after finding pooled object, and implement actual interaction-driven phase logic.
